# Counting ERGM terms

Count each statistic, then check the highlighted answer.

All ties are directed. An **edge** is one arrow; a **dyad** is one unordered node pair.

```{r term-counting-setup, include=FALSE}
library(ergm)
n1 <- igraph::graph_from_edgelist(matrix(c('A','B','B','A','C','D','D','C',
  'A','C','B','E','D','E'), ncol=2, byrow=TRUE), directed=TRUE)
n2 <- igraph::graph_from_edgelist(matrix(c('A','B','A','C','B','C','A','D','B','D','C','D',
  'C','E','D','E','D','F','E','F','F','G','G','E'), ncol=2, byrow=TRUE), directed=TRUE)
n3 <- igraph::graph_from_edgelist(matrix(c('A','B','A','C','A','D','B','D',
  'C','D','D','E','C','E'), ncol=2, byrow=TRUE), directed=TRUE)
xy1 <- matrix(c(-1,1,0,1,-1,0,0,0,1,-.4), ncol=2, byrow=TRUE,
              dimnames=list(LETTERS[1:5],NULL))
xy2 <- matrix(c(-1.8,1.6,0,1.9,.6,.6,-1.2,.4,-.3,-1.1,1.8,-.9,.5,-2.3),
              ncol=2, byrow=TRUE, dimnames=list(LETTERS[1:7],NULL))
xy3 <- matrix(c(-1.5,.4,-.5,1,-.5,-.4,.5,.4,1.5,-.4),
              ncol=2, byrow=TRUE, dimnames=list(LETTERS[1:5],NULL))
pal <- c('#D55E00','#0072B2','#009E73','#CC79A7','#A6761D','#6A3D9A')
s1 <- summary(intergraph::asNetwork(n1) ~ edges + mutual + istar(2) + ostar(2))
s2 <- summary(intergraph::asNetwork(n2) ~ triangle + ctriple)
s3 <- summary(intergraph::asNetwork(n3) ~ esp(1, type='OTP') +
                esp(2, type='OTP') + gwesp(0.5, fixed=TRUE, type='OTP'))

# Separate lanes keep reciprocal arrows and overlapping stars visible.
plot_lanes <- function(g, xy, occurrences, vertex_colors=NULL) {
  ends <- igraph::as_edgelist(g)
  occurrences$key <- apply(ends[occurrences$edge,,drop=FALSE], 1,
    function(x) paste(sort(x), collapse=''))
  occurrences$offset <- 0
  for (key in unique(occurrences$key)) {
    ix <- which(occurrences$key==key)
    occurrences$offset[ix] <- if(length(ix)==1) 0 else seq(-.11,.11,length.out=length(ix))
  }
  par(mar=c(0,0,0,0))
  plot(NA, xlim=range(xy[,1])+c(-.5,.5), ylim=range(xy[,2])+c(-.5,.5),
       asp=1, axes=FALSE, xlab='', ylab='')
  for (k in seq_len(nrow(occurrences))) {
    z <- occurrences[k,]; a <- xy[ends[z$edge,1],]; b <- xy[ends[z$edge,2],]
    d <- (b-a)/sqrt(sum((b-a)^2)); p <- c(-d[2],d[1])
    if (ends[z$edge,1]>ends[z$edge,2]) p <- -p
    start <- a+.20*d+z$offset*p; finish <- b-.20*d+z$offset*p
    arrows(start[1],start[2],finish[1],finish[2],length=.12,
           lwd=if(z$star==0) 2 else if(z$star==2) 5 else 3.5,col=z$color)
  }
  symbols(xy[,1],xy[,2],circles=rep(.16,nrow(xy)),inches=FALSE,
          add=TRUE,bg=if(is.null(vertex_colors)) 'white' else vertex_colors[rownames(xy)],
          fg='#444444',lwd=2)
  text(xy[,1],xy[,2],rownames(xy),font=2,cex=1.4,
       col=if(is.null(vertex_colors)) 'black' else ifelse(vertex_colors[rownames(xy)]==pal[2],'white','black'))
}
plain <- function(g,xy) {
  plot_lanes(g,xy,data.frame(edge=seq_len(igraph::ecount(g)),color='#999999',star=0L))
}
highlight <- function(g,xy,colors) {
  plot_lanes(g,xy,data.frame(edge=seq_len(igraph::ecount(g)),color=colors,
                            star=as.integer(colors!='#999999')))
}
plot_stars <- function(mode) {
  ends <- igraph::as_edgelist(n1); motifs <- list()
  for (v in igraph::V(n1)$name) {
    hits <- which(if(mode=='out') ends[,1]==v else ends[,2]==v)
    if(length(hits)>=2) for(pair in combn(hits,2,simplify=FALSE)) {
      motifs[[length(motifs)+1L]] <- pair
    }
  }
  occurrence <- do.call(rbind,lapply(seq_along(motifs),function(i)
    data.frame(edge=motifs[[i]],color=pal[i],star=i)))
  extras <- setdiff(seq_len(igraph::ecount(n1)),occurrence$edge)
  if(length(extras)) occurrence <- rbind(occurrence,
    data.frame(edge=extras,color='#999999',star=0L))
  plot_lanes(n1,xy1,occurrence)
}
trace_esp <- function(target, paths, partners, color) {
  e <- igraph::as_edgelist(n3); names <- paste(e[,1],e[,2],sep='->')
  cols <- ifelse(names%in%c(target,paths),color,'#999999')
  nodes <- setNames(rep('white',igraph::vcount(n3)),igraph::V(n3)$name)
  nodes[partners] <- color
  plot_lanes(n3,xy3,data.frame(edge=seq_len(igraph::ecount(n3)),color=cols,
    star=ifelse(names==target,2L,as.integer(cols!='#999999'))),nodes)
}
# Apply plot dimensions only to this exercise's chunks.
knitr::opts_hooks$set(term_plot=function(options) {
  if (isTRUE(options$term_plot)) {
    options$fig.width <- 9
    options$fig.height <- 4
    options$out.width <- '68%'
  }
  options
})
```

class: term-count-slide
# Edgewise shared partners: count

For **OTP**, a shared partner of $i\to j$ is a node $k$ on $i\to k\to j$. Which arrows have one partner? Two?

.term-count[`esp(1)` = <span class="term-blank">&nbsp;</span> · `esp(2)` = <span class="term-blank">&nbsp;</span>]

.term-note[`esp(d, type="OTP")` counts arrows with exactly $d$ outgoing two-path shared partners.]

```{r terms-esp-question, term_plot=TRUE}
plain(n3,xy3)
```

---
class: term-count-slide
# One shared partner: answer

C→E has one partner: D, via C→D→E.

.term-count[`esp(1)` = <span class="term-value">`r s3['esp.OTP1']`</span> · `esp(2)` = <span class="term-blank">&nbsp;</span>]

```{r terms-esp-one, term_plot=TRUE}
trace_esp('C->E',c('C->D','D->E'),'D',pal[1])
```

.term-note[The thick arrow is counted; the other colored arrows show the two-path.]

---
class: term-count-slide
# Two shared partners: answer

A→D has two partners: B and C.

.term-count[`esp(1)` = <span class="term-value">`r s3['esp.OTP1']`</span> · `esp(2)` = <span class="term-value">`r s3['esp.OTP2']`</span>]

```{r terms-esp-two, term_plot=TRUE}
trace_esp('A->D',c('A->B','B->D','A->C','C->D'),c('B','C'),pal[2])
```

.term-note[A→B→D and A→C→D. The target arrow contributes **one** to `esp(2)`, not two.]

---
# From ESP to GWESP

With decay $0.5$, an arrow with $k$ OTP shared partners contributes

$$
w(k)=e^{0.5}\left[1-\left(1-e^{-0.5}\right)^k\right].
$$

| Arrow | Partners | ESP statistic | GWESP contribution |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| C→E | D | `esp(1) = 1` | $w(1)=1$ |
| A→D | B, C | `esp(2) = 1` | $w(2)=2-e^{-0.5}\approx1.393$ |

**`gwesp(0.5, fixed=TRUE, type="OTP")` = `r sprintf('%.3f',s3['gwesp.OTP.fixed.0.5'])`**.

The first partner adds 1; the second adds about 0.393. GWESP combines ESP counts with diminishing contributions from additional partners.

---
# Counts and coefficients

These counts are the ERGM's sufficient statistics $g(y)$:

- **Network 1:** `edges` = `r s1['edges']`, `mutual` = `r s1['mutual']`, `ostar(2)` = `r s1['ostar2']`, `istar(2)` = `r s1['istar2']`.
- **Network 2:** `triangle` = `r s2['triangle']`, `ctriple` = `r s2['ctriple']`.
- **Network 3:** `esp(1)` = `r s3['esp.OTP1']`, `esp(2)` = `r s3['esp.OTP2']`, `gwesp(0.5)` = `r sprintf('%.3f',s3['gwesp.OTP.fixed.0.5'])`.

Coefficients weight these statistics in the model. Toggling one arrow can change several statistics at once.

name: estimation_tricks
# Estimation tricks: checkpointing

```{r checkpoint_render_setup, include=FALSE}
set.seed(2026)
# Never overwrite or delete an existing user checkpoint just to render the demo.
if (file.exists("ergm-checkpoint.RData"))
  stop("Existing ergm-checkpoint.RData preserved. Move it aside before rendering this demo.")
network <- intergraph::asNetwork(n1)
network::set.vertex.attribute(network, "group", c("one", "one", "two", "two", "two"))
```

.pull-left-1[
**Five nodes, seven directed ties.**

```{r checkpoint_network, echo=FALSE, fig.width=3.5, fig.height=3, out.width="95%"}
checkpoint_colors <- setNames(
  ifelse(network::get.vertex.attribute(network, "group") == "one", pal[1], pal[2]),
  network::get.vertex.attribute(network, "vertex.names"))
plot_lanes(n1, xy1,
  data.frame(edge=seq_len(igraph::ecount(n1)), color="#777777", star=0L),
  vertex_colors=checkpoint_colors)
```

**Orange:** group one (A/B).<br>
**Blue:** group two (C/D/E).
]

.pull-right-2[
**Overwritten at the start of each MCMLE iteration.**

```{r checkpoint_fit, echo=TRUE, eval=FALSE}
checkpoint_file <- "ergm-checkpoint.RData"

fit <- ergm::ergm(
  network ~ edges + mutual + nodematch("group"),
  control = ergm::control.ergm(
    MCMC.samplesize = 500,
    MCMC.burnin = 100,
    MCMLE.maxit = 5,
    parallel = 0,
    parallel.type = "PSOCK",
    checkpoint = checkpoint_file,
    resume = if (file.exists(checkpoint_file)) checkpoint_file else NULL
  )
)
```

```{r checkpoint_first_output, echo=FALSE}
checkpoint_log <- character()
withCallingHandlers(
  eval(parse(text = knitr::knit_code$get("checkpoint_fit"))),
  message = function(m) {
    checkpoint_log <<- c(checkpoint_log, conditionMessage(m))
    invokeRestart("muffleMessage")
  }
)
cat(grep("^(Iteration |Saving state)", checkpoint_log, value = TRUE), sep = "")
```
]

???
The output chunks run the displayed code and print the save/resume messages.
The network is n1: A/B belong to group one; C/D/E belong to group two.
The controls follow the lecture, with smaller samples, burn-in, and maxit.
parallel=0 runs in the current R process; PSOCK applies when workers are enabled.
The first fit finishes normally. The second run reloads its checkpoint;
no crash is simulated.

---
name: checkpoint_resume
# Estimation tricks: resuming a fit

If RStudio crashes or you stop the fit, rerun the whole code block.
The fit resumes from the last checkpoint.

**Output after rerunning:**

```{r checkpoint_resume_output, echo=FALSE}
checkpoint_log <- character()
withCallingHandlers(
  eval(parse(text = knitr::knit_code$get("checkpoint_fit"))),
  message = function(m) {
    checkpoint_log <<- c(checkpoint_log, conditionMessage(m))
    invokeRestart("muffleMessage")
  }
)
cat(grep("^(Resuming from|Iteration |Saving state)", checkpoint_log, value = TRUE), sep = "")
```

The counter restarts at 1, but the fit uses the saved state.
Use the same network and model.

To start again, delete the checkpoint:

```{r checkpoint_reset, echo=TRUE}
file.remove("ergm-checkpoint.RData")
```

???
ergm 4.12.0 restarts the iteration counter when resuming.
The checkpoint stores the state at the start of an MCMLE iteration.
Work after the last save must be repeated. The file is not the final fitted model.
A fixed filename causes "one argument not used by format" sprintf warnings in
this version; the deck's warning=FALSE hides them.
file.remove deletes the checkpoint created for this example.

# The Intensity of the Effects

---
name: Model_results
description: Interpreting model results
# Interpreting model results
<br>
<br>
<br>

1. $\theta$ > 0 and stat. signif. -> X increases P(1) and decreases P(0)
2. $\theta$ < 0 and stat. signif. -> X decreases P(1) and increases P(0)
3. $\theta$ not stat. signif. -> X does not affect P(1) and P(0)

---
# Binary 

## The sign of $\theta$ provides us with a binary interpretation:

### the probability of the edge forming
- Increases 
- Decreases

.center[![:scale 40%](assets/images/increasesdecreases.jpeg)]

---
# Ok, sure... How much!?

<br>
The number tells us "how much'' ---- Intensity

.center[![:scale 40%](assets/images/intensitypunch.jpeg)]


---
# How much ... or "The extent to which..."

<br>
## x predicts y
<br>

- The odds that x predicts (y) edge formation
- The probability that x predicts (y) edge formation

name: Odds_ratios
description: Odds_ratios
# Odds ratios (Memo: Bootcamp!)

<br>

### ERGMs work with log scale, right? 

### Well, to interpret our coefficients we need to exponentiate it. Makes sense, doesn't it?

<br>

### When you exponentiate you estimate the odds of something to happen -- 

 .red[ODDS = probability of success]
 
### FORMULA

$OR = exp(\theta)$

---
# Odds Ratios meaning (Memo: Bootcamp!)

<br>

### If the coefficients are statistically significant it is possible to comment on the odds of the effect taking place

<br>
## Interpretation:

### An increase of 1 in $X_1$ increases the log odds with $\theta_1$ (log odds) and it makes the odds of the effect taking place $exp(\theta_1)$ times larger.

---
# Consider that...
<br>
<br>
## Odds Ratio is a measure of the strength of association with an exposure and an outcome.

<br>

1. OR > 1 means greater odds of association with the exposure and outcome.
2. OR = 1 means there is no association between exposure and outcome.
3. OR < 1 means there is a lower odds of association between the exposure and outcome.
---
name: Probabilities
description: Probabilities
# Probabilities
<br>
<br>
It measures the probability of an effect taking place
<br>
FORMULA:

$P = \frac{exp(\theta)}{1 + exp(\theta)}$

<br>

WARNING: if you want to use % the result needs to be multiplied by 100.

name: example_inter_res
description: Example for interpreting results
# Back to Florence

## Let's see the intensity of some effects

```{r lab11_01, echo = FALSE}
flo <-SNA4DSData::florentine
fflom <- flo$flomarriage
flom <- intergraph::asNetwork(fflom)
```

.center[![:scale 70%](assets/images/Florence.jpg)]
---
# Dyadic independent model


```{r lab11_02, echo = TRUE}

m <- ergm::ergm(flom ~ edges + nodecov("Wealth"))

```

.center[![:scale 30%](assets/images/Lorenzo_de_Medici.jpg)]
---
# Coefficients 
$\theta$


```{r lab11_03, echo = TRUE}
summary(m)
```
---
# Coefficient interpretation
<br>
### Edges -2.595
$\theta$ < 0 and stat. signif. -> X decreases P(1) and increases P(0)

<br>
### Wealth 0.011

$\theta$ > 0 and stat. signif. -> X increases P(1) and decreases P(0)

<br>

## We still don't know anything about the intensity!!!
---
# Odds Ratios 

$exp(\theta)$


```{r lab11_04, echo = TRUE}
snafun::stat_ef_int(m, type = "odds")
```

### manually estimating edges odds ratios
```{r lab11_05, echo = TRUE}
exp(-2.594929)
```
---
# Odds Interpretation

### edges   0.075

An increase of 1 in .red[the number of edges] increases the log odds with $-2.595$ and it makes the odds of the effect taking place $0.075$ times larger.

OR < 1 means that the odds of forming edges in this network is small.

### nodecov.Wealth 0.011

An increase of 1 in .red[wealth] increases the log odds with $0.011$ and it makes the odds of the effect taking place $1.011$ times larger.

OR > 1 means that the odds of wealth influencing marriage are bigger

OR = 1 means there is little association between wealth influencing marriage.
---
# Probabilities 

$exp(\theta)/ (1 + exp(\theta))$

<br>
```{r lab11_06, echo = TRUE}
snafun::stat_ef_int(m, type = "prob")
```





## manually estimating edges probabilities
```{r lab11_08, echo = TRUE}

exp(-2.594929)/ (1 + exp(-2.594929))

```

---
# Probabilities Interpretation


```{r lab11_07, echo = TRUE}

0.069 * 100
0.503 * 100
```
<br>
### 6.9 % prob of forming edges

small prob, so it is consistent with the OR result
<br>
### 50.3 % prob that wealth predicts marriage

it's a bit more than 1/2 so it is consistent with the OR result

name: Research_flow
description: Approach to carry out research
# Let's organize our research in steps
<br>
1. Literature research/ Questions & Hypotheses (based on the literature) [- data collection]
2. Data Exploration + terms selection
3. Running models (baseline, exploratory models, final model)
4. MCMC diagnostics of the best selected model
5. Goodness of fit
6. Interpreting results
7. Write up about your research telling how this journey went

<br> 

.red[TIP: Rely on these steps for your report]
